artworks.title: The Judgement of Paris
artworks.description: Rubens' Judgement of Paris — the apple that opens the whole Trojan Cycle from wedding quarrel to ten-year war.

artworks.title: The Loves of Paris and Helen
artworks.description: David's Loves of Paris and Helen — the abduction that binds Sparta to Troy and launches the Achaean fleet.

artworks.title: Hector Taking Leave of Andromache
artworks.description: Kauffman's Hector taking leave of Andromache — the Iliad's human centre inside the larger Cycle.

artworks.title: Aeneas' Flight from Troy
artworks.description: Barocci's Flight from Troy — the Cycle's Roman afterlife as Aeneas carries Anchises from the burning city.

artworks.title: Triumphant Achilles
artworks.description: Matsch's Triumphant Achilles — Hector dragged before the walls, the wrath that defines the war's middle books.

popCulture.title: Trojan War
popCulture.description: The Epic Cycle's Trojan arc remains Western literature's founding war — from the apple to the horse, still retold as film, novel and stage.
